summary:
Soraka Program is a health monitoring tool in the form of a website, designed for astronauts in long-duration space missions.  
Since the space environment differs from that on Earth, various hazards, such as altered gravity can greatly affect astronauts' health. Our team Soraka designed this tool to help astronuats monitor their health indicators and track changes over time. 
Astronauts can enter their health data, which includes heart rate, blood glucose level, systolic and diastolic blood preasure, cholesterol level, sleep duration and bone mass. Based on the submitted data, the website generates charts, allowing a better visualization of the health condition of the astronauts. 
Currently, Soraka Program is still a prototype. In the future, we wish to further improve its features, in order to make it more reliable and support the development of space exploration.
details:
How it works

Soraka Program is a web-based monitoring tool designed for astronauts. Astronauts in space missions can manually input their health data into this website, for example blood glucose levels measured at two different time points. After entering the data, the website generates a visual chart, allowing astronauts to compare glucose levels and to evaluate their health condition.

Benefits and Intended impacts

Soraka Program provides an easy and accessible way to visualize health indicators and monitor health status. It allows astronauts to gain a better understanding of their health conditions and encourages them to maintain their well-being. It can also potentially become a widespread database in which NASA can collect useful statistical analysis from astronauts in order to provide them a better space experience.

Tools utilized

Tools:

- Streamlit

- Pandas

- Matplotlib

Coding language: Python 3.14

Creativity

Our team used innovative tools such as Streamlit and Matplotlib to develop a web-based health monitor. It provides a visualization of astronauts' health indicators and a self-assessment towards their own health status.

Factors

Space environment: different gravity fields, space radiation, etc.

Health indicators: heart rate, blood glucose levels, sleep duration, etc.

Data visualization: generates visual charts in order to make the changes more comprehensive
